transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-03-25
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Malik (Redwood AE), Tom Serrano (Redwood SE), Jason Lee (VeridianAI Head of Platform), Priya Nair (VeridianAI ML Eng), Marcus Holt (VeridianAI Infra Lead)

Auto-summary (auto-gen - may be imperfect): Week 2 bench; Redwood shows 1.6x throughput vs baseline for mixed chat workload; median lat improved ~120ms; p99 still 600-800ms on long-context traces; cost delta approx -28% with caching and 4-bit quantization on some configs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, uh quick roll call and we'll get into the bench numbers. Jason?
[00:04] Jason: Mm-hmm, here. Priya here. Marcus on.
[00:07] Aisha: Great. Tom and I are here from Redwood. Tom's got the runbook and the bench artifacts.
[00:12] Tom: Hey all. I dropped the benchmark spreadsheet in the chat earlier, file name rwd-verb-benches-week2.csv, but we'll walk through the highlights.
[00:18] Priya: Saw it, thanks. We pulled the baseline provider logs and tried to line up the same model family but not exactly same quantization, so some noise there.
[00:26] Tom: Right, and we noted that in the assumptions tab. For apples-to-apples we ran on the same model topology with these variants: FP16 baseline, 8-bit and 4-bit quantized for Redwood candidate.
[00:36] Jason: Quick question — when you say throughput increase, like tokens per second or requests per second?
[00:40] Aisha: Good call. Our headline is tokens/sec on a mixed profile: 70% chat-short, 20% medium, 10% long context. So aggregated tokens/sec.
[00:48] Tom: To be specific: baseline provider measured ~210 tokens/sec under your mixed load. Redwood measured ~350 tokens/sec on the same hardware class for the 8-bit run with KV caching enabled. That's the 1.6x number.
[00:58] Priya: Hmm okay, that aligns to what we skimmed. The p50 latency numbers in your sheet look much better, but p95/p99 for some long requests spiked.
[01:05] Tom: Yes. p50 for our config was ~115ms per request (note: this is per-chunk median), p95 around 310ms, and p99 drifted to 720ms on the long-context sample. Those p99 spikes are tied to big context evictions and one-off IO stalls in the experiment env.
[01:18] Marcus: We saw similar tail spikes on the baseline but yours seemed less frequent. Can you describe what you changed?
[01:23] Tom: Two levers: continuous batching with a shorter max-delay (we set max_delay_ms=8ms) and prefix/KV cache warmed for repeated session hits. Also kernel selection — we biased the run for attention kernels that favor medium sequence lengths seen in your traces.
[01:36] Priya: When you say KV cash — kv cash? — is that session caching or something else?
[01:40] Tom: Sorry, KV cache, my bad — transcription — it's the key-value cache for autoregressive decoding. For multi-turn chat it avoids recomputing past tokens. Hit-rate in our run was about 42% given your session reuse patterns.
[01:51] Jason: What's the cost delta? I saw a -28% note but curious about assumptions.
[01:55] Aisha: That -28% is projected unit cost difference per 1M tokens when using 8-bit + caching + batching, versus baseline's FP16 no-cache runs. It includes GPU-hour amortization and network egress for long contexts. We flagged network assumptions in the sheet.
[02:07] Marcus: Any concerns about quality with 8-bit/4-bit? Our generation sanity tests showed occasional token drifts on domain-specific prompts.
[02:13] Tom: Absolutely — we keep a quality safety net. We recommend running a small eval set; for 8-bit we saw negligible regression on your prompts; 4-bit increased hallucination rate on a subset of heavy prompt templates. So if quality is priority we wouldn't push all routes to 4-bit.
[02:26] Priya: Okay, that's useful. Can you share the eval diffs?
[02:28] Tom: Yes, included in the repository under /evals/veridianai_week2_diffs.md — I will make sure it's in the shared folder.
[02:33] Jason: Regarding dedicated vs hosted — what's the path to get consistent p99s?
[02:37] Aisha: Two options: 1) Dedicated pools with pinned capacity and reserved CUDA memory to reduce cold-starts; 2) Hybrid routing where critical routes go to dedicated and the rest hit hosted autoscaling. Dedicated gives stronger p99 guarantees but is more expensive.
[02:49] Marcus: For compliance we also need VPC peering. How did that impact perf in your tests?
[02:54] Tom: In our experience VPC peering adds 5-15ms of network latency depending on region and routing. We modeled a 10ms roundtrip penalty in the sheet for the peered runs. That was included in the p50/p95 numbers labeled "peered".
[03:06] Priya: Any observation on SLOs? Our product team wants 95th under 250ms for chat assistant happy path.
[03:11] Tom: Under your token distribution, with caching and 8-bit quant we hit p95 ~210-240ms on short/medium prompts. Long prompts moved us above that. So routing or fallback for long contexts recommended.
[03:20] Jason: The p99s at 700ms worry the product team though; can we tighten that?
[03:23] Tom: Yes—couple tactics: increase pre-warming for sessions, bump reserved capacity for the hot pool, reduce max-batch size for latency-sensitive routes, and apply token threshold routing so long-context requests get different treatment. We'll propose a config.
[03:34] Aisha: Also a note on batching: aggressive batching improved unit cost by ~14% but increased median by ~20ms. It's a configurable tradeoff.
[03:42] Priya: Right — can we see expected numbers if we prioritize latency (i.e., smaller batches) vs cost?
[03:46] Tom: We'll add a side-by-side scenario in the sheet: conservative (latency-first), balanced, and cost-first. The lake is already in the current tab but we'll make it explicit.
[03:53] Marcus: Any security/regulatory blockers we should flag? We need SOC2 in our vendor list and enterprise audit logs.
[03:59] Aisha: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II; we can share the cert and the security whitepaper. We also offer KMS integration and audit logs for the private deployment. I'll drop that in the folder.
[04:08] Jason: Great, send the security pack. Also curious about failover model — if your primary pool is saturated can you fall back to a cheaper hosted variant?
[04:15] Tom: Yes, smart routing does model fallback to compatible model variants or other regions. We can define a policy that first tries dedicated, then dedicated burst, then hosted compatible model with a slightly higher latency but lower cost.
[04:25] Priya: For the 48-hour soak you mentioned earlier — what's the acceptance criteria?
[04:28] Tom: Good question. Acceptance criteria: 1) No >1% error rate, 2) p95 under 300ms for short routes, 3) cache hit-rate above 30% for repeat sessions, and 4) unit cost within projected -20% vs baseline. We'll codify these and share.
[04:40] Jason: Sounds reasonable. About logs — what level of raw logs do you need? We have concerns about PII.
[04:46] Aisha: We only need length/token distributions and anonymized traces for decoding paths; we don't need user identifiers or raw user content. Describe the strips in the upload instructions and we'll accept hashed ids.
[04:55] Priya: We'll sanitize and deliver by Friday.
[04:58] Tom: Great. Action-wise we'll: 1) upload the per-route breakdown, 2) propose the latency-first config with expected deltas, 3) prepare the soak run plan and acceptance checklist.
[05:08] Marcus: One last perf nit — in your runs, did you see any OOMs when you pushed longer sequences?
[05:12] Tom: We did a controlled OOM once when a very long single request pushed beyond reserved memory, that's what caused a p99 jump in that run. In production we'd enforce request length guardrails or route very long requests to a separate pool.
[05:22] Aisha: Okay, to recap — Redwood to send bench logs + eval diffs + security pack; Veridian AI to send sanitized production traces and confirm peering timeline; both to agree on soak plan.
[05:32] Jason: Thanks, appreciate the clarity. We'll look to confirm internal stakeholders next week.
[05:36] Aisha: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the shared folder links and schedule.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker labels are correct but there are occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash" for KV cache). Some numeric transcriptions may be rounded; see raw logs for precise numbers.
